page.layout: One printed page (right), running text in one column, with a marginal note at the right beside the second paragraph. Running head at top right, page number top centre. Catchword "sunt" at lower right, signature "F 5" at foot. Fragments at the left edge belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: Christus est filius Dei per hypostaticam vnionem homo factus.Ioh.1.1.14. 1.Ioh.4.2. 1.Tim.3.16. Col.2.9.Heb.2.14.16.Rom.1.3.& 9.5.De Chri-sto,cap.4.
Hypostatica vnio est ea vnio assumentis & as-sumptae naturae, qua naturae duae inuicem perfectè di-stinctae, vnà sint hypostasis.1.Tim.3.16.Col.2.9. Heb. 2.16.Gal 4.4.
main_text.l: Naturae vnitae earum- q; distinctio. Vnionis effectus. 2.Cor. 13 4.5. Heb. 1.3.
main_text.p: Natura assumens est{a} ea natura, qua Christus est secunda persona trinitatis, {b} ab ea autem natura assumpta à conceptionis momento sibi vnita {c}in hac hypostasi tantum subsistit,& in æternum gestatur & sustentatur.(a)Phil.2.6.7.Ioh.3.16.& 1.1. 2.3.18.& 5.17. 1,2.& 20.28. 1.Ioh.5.7.20.(b) Luc.1, 35.Gal.4.4. Mat.1.23.(c) Ioh.10.17,18. & 5.26.27. 1, Pet.3.18.
Natura assumpta,est qua Christus est homo no-bis similis per omnia excepto peccato. Hebr.2.14. 15.16.17.& 4.15.Rom.8.3.
main_text.head: Huius naturae proprietates

page.notes: The marginal note at right reads "De Christo, cap.4." with a hyphen at the line end. The running head is partly worn; "De Christe" is uncertain at its last letter. The text is damaged at the start of the page where the previous page's edge shows; the catchword "sunt" is at the foot and is also the start of the next line, so it may be duplicated. The word "Huius naturae proprietates" is placed as a heading but is a running sentence line; the line "sunt" below it is the catchword.
